properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-21: "as I state quite often, using reflow2 on reflow2 is our first proof of concept; however, reflow2 is a tool for other projects. that being said, should we introduce an /optimize skill (that would occur after black boxes have been identified) that any project could do on its modules?"

⭐ THE UNUSUAL THING ABOUT THIS IDEA IS THAT THE PROCEDURE WAS ALREADY RUN ONCE, BY HAND, AN HOUR BEFORE HE ASKED. That is not a coincidence to note in passing — it is the only evidence available about whether the skill would have content, and it is first-hand rather than imagined.

THE RUN, in the order it actually happened:
  1. MEASURED WHERE THE TIME WENT. 191.8 s across 127 test binaries. The worst thing was not the biggest file but the worst COST PER UNIT OF WORK — 2.44 s/test in one file against a 0.92 s median for a whole binary.
  2. FOUND THE CAUSE BY MEASURING, NOT GUESSING. open_in_memory 41.3 ms vs an add_capability write at 54.7 us: construction cost 750x a write. Cause: eleven include_str!'d YAML documents re-parsed on every construction.
  3. WROTE THE BUDGET DOWN BEFORE TOUCHING CODE. `con:graph-construction-is-setup-not-work`, 1 ms, derived rather than picked.
  4. OPTIMISED. Cached the parse.
  5. RE-MEASURED AGAINST THE BUDGET AND STOPPED. Suite 191.8 s -> 96.5 s.
  6. MADE THE MEASUREMENT DURABLE.
  7. PAID THE GUARDS THAT FIRED.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE STEP THAT EARNED ITS PLACE: THE BUDGET MADE THE WORK STOP
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

First re-measurement after the fix read 2.79 ms — a 14.8x speedup AND OVER BUDGET. Without a number written down beforehand, "14.8x faster" is exactly where optimisation stops and everyone feels good. The warm figure was 266 us, under budget, so the work stopped there — leaving the obvious next move (Arc instead of cloning the schema, which would recover 252 of those 266 us) UNDONE, because it needs a dependency's API in another repo. **The budget produced a defensible stopping point at a repo boundary.** That is the anti-over-engineering mechanism working, and it is the strongest argument that the skill has real content rather than being a checklist.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 TWO THINGS BIT DURING THE RUN, AND BOTH BELONG IN THE SKILL
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(1) **A DURATION ASSERTION IN A PARALLEL SUITE MEASURES CONTENTION, NOT CODE.** The first durable test asserted "a warm construction takes under 5 ms". Alone: 266 us, comfortable. Inside `cargo test --workspace` with dozens of binaries competing: **6 ms, and the gate failed.** The usual response is to raise the threshold until it stops complaining, which RETIRES THE GATE WITHOUT ANYONE DECIDING TO. The fix was to assert a RATIO — cold construction versus warm — which survives contention because both halves are slowed equally, and which asserts the thing that actually broke: the parse happening once. ⇒ **AN OPTIMISATION GUARD SHOULD ASSERT THE STRUCTURE THAT MAKES THE CODE FAST, NOT THE TIME IT TAKES.** Time is a property of the machine as much as of the program.

(2) **THE OPTIMISATION TRIPPED A DESIGN RULE, AND PAYING IT WAS ONE PARAGRAPH.** Caching the parse in a `LazyLock` is a process-global, and `no_per_design_process_globals` refused it. That test's own words: *"the door closes one convenient static at a time, each individually reasonable."* Mine was one of those. The rule's question — would a second design open in this process need a different value? — had a clean answer (the YAML is compiled in; it is a fact about the BINARY), and the cost of the global was stating it. ⇒ **OPTIMISATION IS WHERE ARCHITECTURAL RULES GET QUIETLY TRADED AWAY FOR SPEED**, one reasonable exception at a time, and a skill that does not say so is missing the thing most worth saying.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 AND HIS PRECONDITION IS THE PART I WOULD PUSH BACK ON
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

He frames it as occurring AFTER black boxes have been identified. Measured earlier today, optimising one module needs THREE things and the contract is only one:
  (i)   a WALL, so a change inside cannot leak out       — 0 of 10 subsystems publish a contract
  (ii)  a TARGET, so you know when to stop                — 1 Constraint before today, and not a budget
  (iii) a MEASUREMENT, so you can tell if you improved it — no benches, no criterion, not one Instant::now()

**AND THE RUN ABOVE HAPPENED WITH (i) ABSENT.** No contract existed for the module optimised, and the work was still correct, bounded and successful — because (ii) and (iii) were supplied. You CANNOT optimise with a wall and no measurement; you can only change things and believe you improved them. So the skill does NOT need to wait for black boxes, and gating it on them would withhold the cheapest of the three returns until the most expensive one is finished. ⇒ **THE PRECONDITION IS A TARGET AND A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CONTRACT.** A contract makes optimisation SAFER (a change that leaks is caught); it does not make it possible.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE OPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(a) A SERVED `optimize` SKILL, gated on a target and a measurement rather than on black boxes. Its content is the ORDER and the REFUSALS, not the technique: measure before guessing; write the budget BEFORE the code; re-measure against the budget rather than against the old number; assert structure not duration; and when a rule refuses your change, pay it in prose rather than weakening it. CHEAPEST, and it is the leg reflow2 is best at. HONEST LIMIT: **ONE RUN IS NOT A PROCEDURE.** Everything above came from a single optimisation, in Rust, on a test suite, on one machine. A skill generalised from n=1 is a story about one afternoon wearing the costume of a method.

(b) THE THIRD LEG FIRST — a detector. `Constraint` + `budget_report` is the TOOL leg and it exists; a skill would be the INSTRUCTION leg; nothing notices a project that has optimised without a budget, or a Constraint nobody ever measured against. Candidate finding: *a Constraint with no contribution recorded* — a budget stated and never checked, which is the shape a target takes when it decays into decoration.

(c) DO NOTHING YET, AND RUN IT AGAIN FIRST. Optimise a second thing — ideally in a different language, or on something that is not a test suite — and see which of the seven steps survive contact. The strongest argument for waiting is that the two lessons above were BOTH discovered by doing rather than by thinking, and a second run is the only way to find the third.

(d) FOLD IT INTO AN EXISTING SKILL rather than minting a twenty-first. `check-health` and `impact-check` already run after a change. Cheapest on surface area; loses the thing that makes the procedure work, which is that it is a SEQUENCE with a step that must come first.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT IS NOT KNOWN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Whether any of the seven steps is reflow2-specific. Step 1 needed cargo's per-binary timings parsed out of test output — a project with no such output would need something else entirely, and a skill cannot supply it. The GENERIC part may be only steps 3, 5 and 6 (state the budget, re-measure against it, make it durable), with steps 1, 2 and 4 being "do the obvious thing for your stack". If that is the whole content, it is a short skill — and possibly a better one for being short.
properties.name: OPEN — should `optimize` be a served skill? The procedure was run once by hand and two of its lessons were found by doing, not thinking
properties.rationale:
═══ UPDATE 2026-08-31 — THE PREMISE OF THIS QUESTION HAS MOVED, AND THE DECISION TEXT ABOVE IS AS ANTHONY LEFT IT ON 2026-08-21. Nothing above was rewritten; this is appended so a reader meets the correction rather than the stale framing. ═══

WHAT HAPPENED SINCE. The skill was BUILT and IS SERVED — `optimize/SKILL.md`, carried in the served catalogue and in `list_skills`, with ten of its obligations pinned by `tools/skill_lint.py` in CI (budget precedes the code; the number is derived not picked; measures against the budget not the starting point; stops when met; records what was left undone; guards assert structure not duration; names the raise-the-threshold failure; refuses to weaken a rule for speed; allows the answer "nothing here"; states how little it has been run). So option (a) was effectively taken.

⭐ AND IT HAS NOW BEEN RUN TWICE, NOT ONCE. This node's central caveat — "ONE RUN IS NOT A PROCEDURE... a skill generalised from n=1 is a story about one afternoon wearing the costume of a method" — is n=2 as of the 2026-08-21 granularity and sweep work. Three budget Constraints now exist, and MEASURED 2026-08-31 all three are MET and GUARDED, by guards that assert structure exactly as the skill demands:
    con:graph-construction-is-setup-not-work      1 ms      the_first_construction_pays_for_the_parse_and_the_rest_do_not (cold/warm ratio)
    con:granularity-reads-scale-with-artifacts    N+2 reads the_reading_costs_one_store_read_per_artifact_plus_a_constant (a count)
    con:a-sweep-builds-its-network-a-fixed-number 4 builds  the_sweep_does_not_scale_with_its_candidates (a count)
Both budgets this node's siblings recorded as UNMET at the time of writing (41x and 2.5x over) have since been met. Nobody had re-read them, which is why this is being written down.

🛑 OPTION (c) IS THE ONE STILL OPEN, AND ANTHONY IS NOW PROPOSING EXACTLY IT. Its words were: "DO NOTHING YET, AND RUN IT AGAIN FIRST. Optimise a second thing — ideally in a different language, or on something that is NOT A TEST SUITE — and see which of the seven steps survive contact." Of the three runs to date, two targeted a test suite or a structural read count and only the sweep touched the product surface. His 2026-08-31 proposal to sweep the subsystems for performance is a candidate third run against something that is not a test suite, which is the evidence option (c) asked for.

🛑 OPTION (b) REMAINS UNBUILT AND IS THE MISSING THIRD LEG. It named the detector precisely: "a Constraint with no contribution recorded — a budget stated and never checked, which is the shape a target takes when it decays into decoration." The TOOL leg exists (`Constraint` + `budget_report`) and the INSTRUCTION leg now exists (the served skill), but nothing notices a project that optimised without a budget, or a budget nobody ever measured against. On the three-legs reading, that absence is the likeliest reason the skill sees little use — including here.

⚠️ WHAT THIS UPDATE DOES NOT SETTLE: whether any of the seven steps is reflow2-specific, which this node listed under "what is not known" and which two further runs on the same project cannot answer. That still needs a run somewhere that is not this repository.
